**Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 30, verses 17–19:**

His saying: ﴿So glorify God when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning.﴾ Regarding the naming of the prayer as tasbih (glorification), there are two views:

First: because of what it includes of the mention of glorification (tasbih) in the bowing (ruku') and prostration (sujud).

Second: it is derived from al-subha (the rosary/voluntary prayer), and al-subha means prayer. From this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "There will be for you a subha on the Day of Resurrection," i.e., a prayer.

His saying: ﴿when you enter the evening﴾ means the prayers of Maghrib and 'Isha', as said by Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Jubayr and al-Dahhak.

﴿and when you enter the morning﴾ is the Subh prayer, according to their saying as well.

﴿And to Him belongs praise in the heavens and the earth﴾: regarding this there are two views:

First: praise belongs to God for His blessings and favours.

Second: it refers to the prayer, because it is specific to the recitation of praise (al-hamd) in al-Fatiha.

﴿and in the afternoon﴾ means the 'Asr prayer.

﴿and when you enter the noon﴾ means the Zuhr prayer. The reason He specified the night prayer with the name of glorification and the day prayer with the name of praise is that a person during the day moves through states that necessitate praising God for them, whereas at night he is in seclusion, which necessitates declaring God free of evils in it. Therefore praise became more specific to the day, so the day prayer was named by it, and glorification became more specific to the night, so the night prayer was named by it.

The difference between al-masa' (evening) and al-'ashiy (late afternoon) is that al-masa' is the appearance of darkness after sunset, while al-'ashiy is the end of the day as the sun inclines toward setting; it is derived from 'asha al-'ayn (dimness of the eye), which is the diminishing of light in the viewer, like the diminishing of the sun's light. Thus this verse comprises the times of the five prayers. Sufyan narrated from 'Asim that Nafi' ibn al-Azraq asked Ibn 'Abbas: "Do you find the five prayers in the Book of God?" So he recited this verse.

Yahya ibn Salam said: Every prayer mentioned in the Book of God before the night in which the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was taken on the Night Journey is not among the five prayers, because they were enjoined on the night he was taken on the Journey, which was a year before the Hijra. He said: This verse was revealed after the Night of the Journey and before the Hijra.

﴿He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living﴾: regarding this there are four interpretations:

The first: He brings the living human out of the dead drop (nutfa) and brings the dead drop out of the living human. This was said by Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, Mujahid, Qatada and Ibn Jubayr.

The second: He brings the believer out of the disbeliever and brings the disbeliever out of the believer. This was said by 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may God be pleased with him) and al-Zuhri, and al-Aswad ibn 'Abd Yaghuth narrated it from the Prophet (ﷺ).

The third: He brings the chick out of the egg and brings the egg out of the chicken. This was said by 'Ikrima.

The fourth: He brings the palm tree out of the date-stone and brings the date-stone out of the palm tree; and the ear of grain out of the seed and the seed out of the ear. This was said by Ibn Malik and al-Suddi.

It may also admit a fifth: He brings the clever and intelligent out of the incapable and dull, and brings the incapable and dull out of the clever and intelligent.

﴿and revives the earth after its death﴾, meaning with vegetation, because it is the life of its people, so it becomes life for it.

It may also be understood, secondly, that it means the abundance of its people, because they revive its dead places and rebuild its ruins.

﴿Thus you will be brought forth﴾, i.e., just as He revives the earth by bringing forth vegetation and revives the dead, so He will give you life by resurrection.

In this is evidence for the validity of analogical reasoning (qiyas).

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 30, verses 20–21:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And among His signs is that He created for you spouses from among yourselves﴾ has two interpretations:

One of them: He created Hawwa' (Eve) from the rib of Adam. This was said by Qatadah.

The second: that He created all spouses from their likes among men and women. This was said by ʿAli ibn ʿIsa.

﴿That you may find tranquility in them﴾: that you may be at ease with them, because He placed between the spouses [of] intimacy that He did not place between others.

﴿And He placed between you affection and mercy﴾. On this there are four interpretations:

The first: that affection (mawaddah) is love, and mercy (rahmah) is compassion and tenderness. This was said by al-Suddi.

The second: that affection is sexual intercourse (jima') and mercy is offspring (walad). This was said by al-Hasan.

The third: that affection is love for the elder and mercy is tenderness toward the young. This was said by al-Kalbi.

The fourth: that they are mutual compassion between the spouses. This was said by Muqatil.

(p-306) ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect﴾ admits of two meanings:

One of them: they reflect upon the fact that they have a Creator who is worthy of worship.

The second: they reflect upon resurrection after death.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 30, verses 22–23:

His words: ﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾. In this there are two views:

One: because of the signs and lessons they contain.

The second: because of the inability of creation to bring about the like of them.

﴿And the diversity of your tongues and your colours﴾. In this there are two views:

One: the diversity of your tongues in speech. The Arabs have a speech, the Persians have a speech, and the Romans have a speech.

And your colours: white, black, and red. This was said by al-Suddi. Wahb ibn Munabbih, in al-Mubtada', related that the total number of languages is seventy-two. Of them, among the descendants of Sam ibn Nuh are nineteen languages, among the descendants of Ham seventeen languages, and among the descendants of Yafith thirty-six languages.

The second view: the diversity of your tongues refers to tone and voice, so that no two voices of brothers born of the same mother and father are alike; and your colours refers to form, so that people are not confused in recognition, in marriage, and in rights.

﴿Indeed in that are signs for those of knowledge﴾. Ibn 'Isa said: [this refers to] the jinn and mankind.

Hafs related from 'Asim, reading ﴿lil-'alimin﴾ with a kasra on the lam, meaning all those who have knowledge (ulama').

His words: ﴿And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day, and your seeking of His bounty﴾. In this there are two views:

One: that night and day together are a time for sleep and a time for seeking His bounty, because among people there are those who conduct their livelihood by night and sleep by day.

The second: that night is the time of sleep and day is the time for seeking His bounty, and the sentence would be construed as: [And among His signs is your sleep by night, and your seeking of His bounty by day.]

Regarding seeking His bounty there are two views:

One: trade, said by Mujahid.

The second: activity and labour.

So He made sleep at night a proof of death, and activity by day a proof of resurrection.

﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who hear﴾. In this there are three views:

One: they hear the truth and follow it.

The second: they hear admonition and fear it.

The third: they hear the Qur'an and affirm it.

**Commentary of al-Mawardi (*al-Nukat wa al-Uyun*) on Surah 30, verses 24–25:**

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And among His signs is that He shows you the lightning, [causing] fear and hope﴾. Regarding this there are four interpretations:

First: [it is] fear for the traveler and hope for the resident. This was said by Qatadah.

Second: [it is] fear of the thunderbolts and hope for the rain. This was said by al-Dahhak.

Third: [it is] fear of the hail, lest it destroy the crops, and hope for the rain, lest it give life to the crops. This was related by Yahya ibn Salam.

Fourth: [it is] fear that the lightning will be *khulab* (dry lightning, without rain), and hope that it will bring rain. This was mentioned by Ibn Bahr, who recited the poet's verse:

> Let not your lightning be dry lightning;
> Indeed, the best lightning is that which comes with rain.

The Arabs say: when forty flashes of lightning follow one another, it will rain. Al-Mutanabbi alluded to this in his saying:(p-308)

> I may approach the waters without provision,
> Except for my counting of the lightning clouds for them.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And among His signs is that the heaven and the earth stand by His command﴾. Regarding this there are two interpretations:

One: that they *takun* (exist).

Two: that they *tathbutu* (remain firm).

﴿By His command﴾ has two interpretations:

One: by His management and His wisdom.

Two: by His permission to them to stand without pillars.

﴿Then, when He calls you with a call from the earth﴾, that is, while you are dead in your graves.

﴿Behold, you come out﴾, that is, from your graves, resurrected for the Day of Resurrection.

Qatadah said: He calls them from the sky, and they come out of the earth.

Then, regarding this there are three interpretations:

First: that He brings them out with that which is like a call and like His saying "Be, and it is," said by Ibn Isa.

Second: that He brings them out with a call that He calls them with, said by Qatadah.

Third: that He brings them out with the second blast and makes it a call for them.

It seems that this is the saying of Yahya ibn Salam.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 30, verse 26–27:

His saying: ﴿Everything is devoutly obedient to Him﴾. Concerning this there are six interpretations:

First: they are obedient (muti'un). This was said by Mujahid.

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Every letter of the Qur'an in which qunut (devout obedience) is mentioned means obedience."

Second: they are those who pray (musallun). This was said by Ibn 'Abbas.

Third: they acknowledge servitude (muqirrun bil-'ubudiyya). This was said by 'Ikrima, Abu Malik and al-Suddi.

Fourth: everything stands before Him on the Day of Resurrection (qa'im). This was said by al-Rabi' ibn Anas.

Fifth: everything bears witness that it is His servant (qa'im bil-shahada annahu 'abd lahu). This was said by al-Hasan.

Sixth: it means the sincere (al-mukhlis). This was said by Ibn Jubayr.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He it is who originates creation, then repeats it﴾. As for the origination of His creation, it is by its formation in the womb before birth; and as for its repetition, it is His giving life after death by the second blast for resurrection. He made what is known of the beginning of creation a proof for what is hidden of its repetition, reasoning from the witnessed to the unseen.

Then He confirmed this with His saying: ﴿And it is easier for Him﴾. Concerning this there are three aspects:

First: the repetition of creation is easier than its initial production, because in the beginning they are transferred from a drop (nutfa), then a clinging clot ('alaqa), then a lump of flesh (mudgha), then bone, then they return as a suckling infant, then a weaned child. In the repetition, a call is made to them and they stand up upright. This is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas.

Second: its meaning is "and it is easy for Him," so "easier" (ahwan) is placed in the position of "easy" (hayyin), as in the saying of al-Farazdaq:

Indeed He who raised the sky built for us a house whose pillars are mightier and taller.

That is: its pillars are mighty and tall.

Regarding the interpretation of "easier" there are two views:

One: "easier" (aysar). This was said by Ibn 'Abbas.

Second: "easier" (as-hal). Ibn Shajara recited the verse of the poet:

And it became easy for Asma' that the distance grew far, while the lovesick one yearns for her and longs.

That is, she is easier for him. And al-Rabi' ibn Haytham, concerning His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is easier for Him﴾, said: nothing is difficult for God.

﴿And His is the highest likeness﴾, that is, the highest attribute.

Concerning this there are three sayings:

First: that there is nothing like Him. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas.

Second: it is the testimony that there is no god but God. This was said by Qatada.

Third: that He gives life and causes death. This was said by al-Dahhak.

It may also include a fourth meaning (and He knows best): that it is the totality of the attributes peculiar to Him, in which no created being shares.

﴿In the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, there is no god in them other than Him.

﴿And He is the Mighty﴾. Concerning this there are two views:

One: unassailable in His power.

Second: in His retribution.

﴿The Wise﴾. Concerning this there are two views:

One: in His management of His affair, and this is the meaning of the saying of Abu al-'Aliya.

Second: in His establishing proof and argument against His servants. This was said by Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 30, verses 28–29:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He has coined for you a parable from yourselves﴾. There is disagreement over the reason why God coined this parable for them, in three opinions:

The first: because the polytheists associated others with Him in worship. This is the view of Qatadah.

The second: because the talbiyah (the invocation recited during pilgrimage) of the Quraysh in the Jahiliyyah was: "Here I am, O God, here I am. Here I am, You have no partner, except a partner who is Yours, You own him and what he owns." So God revealed this verse. This is the view of Ibn Jubayr.

The third: because they would not give inheritance to their clients (mawali), so God coined this parable. This is the view of al-Suddi.

Its interpretation: your slaves do not share with you in your property, because you own them. God is more worthy that none of His creation should share with Him in worship, since He is their owner and their creator.

﴿You fear them as you fear one another, your own selves﴾. In this there are three aspects:

The first: you fear that they will share with you in your wealth, just as you fear that from your partners. This is the view of Abu Mijlaz.

The second: you fear that they will inherit from you, just as you fear your heirs. This is the view of al-Suddi.

The third: you fear their blame, just as you fear one another. This is the view of Yahya ibn Salam.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿فَأقِمْ وجْهَكَ﴾ فِيهِ ثَلاثَةُ أوْجُهٍ:

أحَدُها: قَصْدَكَ.

الثّانِي: دِينَكَ، قالَهُ الضَّحّاكُ.

الثّالِثُ: عَمَلَكَ، قالَهُ الكَلْبِيُّ.

﴿لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفًا﴾ فِيهِ سِتَّةُ تَأْوِيلاتٍ:

أحَدُها: مُسْلِمًا، وهَذا قَوْلُ الضَّحّاكِ.

والثّانِي: مُخْلِصًا، وهَذا قَوْلُ خُصَيْفٍ.

الثّالِثُ: مُتَّبِعًا، قالَهُ مُجاهِدٌ.

الرّابِعُ: مُسْتَقِيمًا، قالَهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ كَعْبٍ.

الخامِسُ: حاجًّا، قالَهُ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ.

السّادِسُ: مُؤْمِنًا بِالرُّسُلِ كُلِّهِمْ، قالَهُ أبُو قِلابَةَ.

(p-٣١٢)﴿فِطْرَتَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي فَطَرَ النّاسَ عَلَيْها﴾ فِيها تَأْوِيلانِ:

أحَدُهُما: صَنْعَةَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي خَلَقَ النّاسَ عَلَيْها، قالَهُ الطَّبَرِيُّ.

الثّانِي: دِينَ اللَّهِ الَّذِي فَطَرَ خَلْقَهُ عَلَيْهِ، قالَهُ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ والضَّحّاكُ والكَلْبِيُّ، يُرِيدُ بِهِ الإسْلامَ. وقَدْ رَوى عَطاءٌ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ (ﷺ) أنَّهُ قالَ: «مِن فِطْرَةِ إبْراهِيمَ السُّواكُ». ومِن قَوْلِ كَعْبِ بْنِ مالِكٍ:

؎ إنْ تَقْتُلُونا فَدِينُ اللَّهِ فِطْرَتُنا والقَتْلُ في الحَقِّ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ تَفْضِيلُ

﴿لا تَبْدِيلَ لِخَلْقِ اللَّهِ﴾ فِيهِ ثَلاثَةُ تَأْوِيلاتٍ:

أحَدُها: لا تَبْدِيلَ لِدِينِ اللَّهِ، قالَهُ مُجاهِدٌ وقَتادَةُ.

الثّانِي: لا تَغْيِيرَ لِخَلْقِ اللَّهِ مِنَ البَهائِمِ بِأنْ يُخْصِيَ فُحُولَها، قالَهُ عُمَرُ بْنُ الخَطّابِ وابْنُ عَبّاسٍ وعِكْرِمَةُ.

الثّالِثُ: لا تَبْدِيلَ خالِقٍ غَيْرَ اللَّهِ فَيَخْلُقُ كَخَلْقِ اللَّهِ، لِأنَّهُ خالِقٌ يَخْلُقُ، وغَيْرُهُ مَخْلُوقٌ لا يَخْلُقُ، وهو مَعْنى قَوْلِ ابْنِ بَحْرٍ.

وَيَحْتَمِلُ رابِعًا: لا يَشْقى مَن خَلَقَهُ سَعِيدًا، ولا يَسْعَدُ مَن خَلَقَهُ شَقِيًّا.

﴿ذَلِكَ الدِّينُ القَيِّمُ﴾ فِيهِ تَأْوِيلانِ:

الرّابِعُ: تائِبِينَ إلَيْهِ مِنَ الذُّنُوبِ، ومِنهُ قَوْلُ أبِي قَيْسِ بْنِ الأسْلَتِ:

وَفِي أصْلِ الإنابَةِ قَوْلانِ:

أحَدُهُما: أنَّ أصْلَهُ القَطْعُ، ومِنهُ أُخِذَ اسْمُ النّابِ لِأنَّهُ قاطِعٌ، فَكَأنَّ الإنابَةَ هي الِانْقِطاعُ إلى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وجَلَّ بِالطّاعَةِ.

أحَدُها: أنَّهُمُ اليَهُودُ، قالَهُ قَتادَةُ.

الثّانِي: أنَّهُمُ اليَهُودُ والنَّصارى، قالَهُ مَعْمَرٌ.

الثّالِثُ: أنَّهُمُ الخَوارِجُ مِن هَذِهِ الأُمَّةِ، وهَذا قَوْلُ أبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، ورَواهُ أبُو أُمامَةَ مَرْفُوعًا.

الرّابِعُ: أنَّهم أصْحابُ الأهْواءِ والبِدَعِ، رَوَتْهُ عائِشَةُ مَرْفُوعًا.

(p-٣١٤)﴿وَكانُوا شِيَعًا﴾ فِيهِ وجْهانِ:

أحَدُهُما: فِرَقًا، قالَهُ الكَلْبِيُّ.

الثّانِي: أدْيانًا، قالَهُ مُقاتِلٌ.

وَيَحْتَمِلُ ثالِثًا: أنَّهم أنْصارُ الأنْبِياءِ وأتْباعُهم.

﴿كُلُّ حِزْبٍ﴾ أيْ فِرْقَةٍ.

﴿بِما لَدَيْهِمْ فَرِحُونَ﴾ أيْ بِما عِنْدَهم مِنَ الضَّلالَةِ.

﴿فَرِحُونَ﴾ فِيهِ ثَلاثَةُ أوْجُهٍ:

أحَدُها: مَسْرُورُونَ، قالَهُ الجُمْهُورُ.

الثّانِي: مُعْجَبُونَ، قالَهُ ابْنُ زَيْدٍ.

الثّالِثُ: مُتَمَسِّكُونَ، قالَهُ مُجاهِدٌ.

(p-315) His saying: ﴿Or have We sent down to them an authority (sultanan)?﴾ Concerning this there are four interpretations:

First: it means a book. This is said by al-Dahhak.

Second: an excuse. This is said by Qatadah.

Third: a proof (burhanan). This is the meaning of the saying of al-Suddi and ʿAta'.

Fourth: a messenger. This is related by Ibn ʿIsa as a possibility.

﴿So he speaks of what they used to associate with Him.﴾ This may bear two meanings:

One: its meaning is that he informs about it.

Second: it argues for it.

His saying: ﴿And when We cause people to taste mercy﴾ concerning this there are two interpretations:

One: that it is well-being and abundance. This is said by Yahya ibn Salam.

Second: blessing and rain. This is related by al-Naqqash.

It may also be that it is security and ease.

﴿they rejoice in it﴾ i.e., in the mercy.

﴿And if an evil afflicts them﴾ concerning this there are two interpretations:

One: affliction and punishment. This is said by Mujahid.

Second: a lack of rain. This is said by al-Suddi.

It may also, as a third possibility, mean fear and caution.

﴿for what their hands have sent forth﴾ i.e., for their sins.

﴿then behold, they despair﴾ concerning this there are two interpretations:

One: that despair is hopelessness of mercy and relief. This is said by the majority (al-jumhur).

Second: that despair is abandoning the obligations of Allah in times of ease. This is said by al-Hasan.

(p-316) His saying: ﴿So give to the near of kin his due﴾ — regarding them there are two views.

One: they are the man's relatives, that he should join the ties of kinship (silat al-rahim) with his wealth and his person. This was said by al-Hasan and Qatadah.

Two: they are the close relatives of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his family, namely the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib, who are given their due from the spoils (ghanimah) and the fay'. This was said by al-Suddi.

﴿And the needy﴾ is the one who does not find his sufficiency.

﴿And the wayfarer﴾ — regarding it there are two views:

One: the traveler. This was said by Mujahid. If he is in need, his right is in the zakah; and if he is not in need, it is an act of righteousness and kindness (birr wa silah).

Two: that it is the guest who alights upon you. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Jubayr and Qatadah. If you feed him, it is an act of righteousness and kindness, and it is not permissible that it be from zakah, whether he is in need or not.

If you give him money, it is permissible, when he is poor, for it to be from zakah, and it is not permissible if he is wealthy.

His saying: ﴿And whatever you give in usury (riba) so that it may increase in the wealth of people, it does not increase with Allah﴾ — regarding it there are three views:

One: it is the man who gives a gift in order to be repaid with something better. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid.

Two: it concerns a man who accompanied another on a journey and served him, and the one served gave him a portion of his profit in exchange for his service, not for the sake of Allah. This was said by al-Sha'bi.

Three: it concerns a man who gives wealth to a relative of his so that he becomes wealthy through it, and he does not do it seeking the reward of Allah. This was said by Ibrahim.

The meaning of His saying ﴿it does not increase with Allah﴾ is that there is no reward for it with Allah.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "There are two kinds of riba: one is lawful and the other is unlawful. What you exchange among yourselves is lawful, and it does not reach Allah."

(p-317) ﴿And whatever you give in zakah, seeking the Face of Allah﴾ — that is, seeking the reward of Allah. Regarding it there are two views:

One: that it is the obligatory zakah, and this is the apparent meaning.

Two: that it is charity (sadaqah). This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and al-Suddi.

﴿Those are the ones who receive multiplication﴾ — regarding it there are two views:

One: their good deeds are multiplied, because whoever comes with a good deed will have ten like it. This was said by al-Suddi.

Two: their wealth is multiplied in this world by increase in it. al-Kalbi said: "No man's wealth decreases through zakah."

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 30, verse 41–42:

His saying: ﴿Corruption has appeared on land and sea﴾. Regarding ﴿al-fasad (corruption)﴾ there are four opinions:

First: it is polytheism (shirk), said by al-Suddi.

Second: it is the committing of sins (ma'asi), said by Abu al-'Aliyah.

Third: it is the drought of rain (qahṭ al-matar), said by Yahya ibn Sallam.

Fourth: the corruption of the land is the killing of Adam's son of his brother, and the corruption of the sea is the seizing of the ship by force (ghasban).

And it may be a fifth: that the appearance of corruption is the rulers of evil (wulat al-su').

﴿On land and sea﴾ here has four opinions:

First: that "the land" (al-barr) means the deserts (al-fayafi) and "the sea" (al-bahr) means the towns (al-qura), said by 'Ikrimah, who said: the Arabs call the great cities "seas" (bihar).

Second: "the land" means the people of the tents (ahl al-'amud) and "the sea" means the people of the villages and the countryside (al-rif), said by Qatadah.

Third: that "the land" is the desert dwelling of the Bedouins (badiyat al-a'rab), said by al-Dahhak, and "the sea" is the islands (al-jaza'ir), said by 'Ata'.

Fourth: that "the land" is what is among the cities and towns not on a river, and "the sea" is what is on the bank of a river, said by Ibn 'Abbas.

For those who delve into the subtleties of meanings there are two aspects:

One: that "the land" is the self (nafs) and "the sea" is the heart (qalb).

Second: that "the land" is the tongue (lisan) and "the sea" is the heart (qalb),

because what is upon the tongue is apparent and what is in the heart is hidden.

And this is far-fetched.

﴿By what the hands of people have earned﴾. al-Suddi said: by what they did of sins and acquired of wrongdoings.

﴿That He may let them taste some of what they have done﴾ of sins, a hastened recompense in this world and a deferred recompense in the Hereafter; so the punishment of this world became some of the recompense.

﴿So that they may return﴾. Regarding this there are three aspects:

First: they may return from sins, said by Abu al-'Aliyah.

Second: they may return to the truth, said by Ibrahim.

Third: "he may return" (yarji'u) from after them, said by al-Hasan.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 30, verses 43–45:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So set your face toward the upright religion﴾ has two interpretations:

One of them: Set your face toward monotheism (al-tawhid). This was said by al-Suddi.

The second: Remain upright in the straight religion, bringing its adherent to Paradise. This was said by Ibn 'Isa.

﴿Before there comes a Day which will not be turned back from Allah﴾ means the Day of Resurrection.

﴿That Day they will be divided﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: its meaning is that they will separate (yatafarraqun). The poet said:

"We were like the two companions of Judhayma for a period of time, until it was said to him: 'Let them separate (yatasaddaa)!'"

(p-319) That is, they will never separate.

It may also bear a second meaning: that on the Day of Resurrection the terrors will split them apart (yusaddi'uhum).

**Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 30, verses 46–47:**

His saying: ﴿And among His signs is that He sends the winds as bearers of good news﴾. Al-Dahhak said: "With rain."

It may also bear a second meaning: with the abundance of the time and the health of bodies.

Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: "Everything in the Qur'an that mentions *al-riyah* (the winds, plural) is mercy, and everything in the Qur'an that mentions *al-rih* (the wind, singular) is punishment."

Abdullah ibn Umar said: "The winds are eight: four of them are mercy and four are punishment. As for the mercy, they are *al-nashirat* (the spreading ones), *al-mubashshirat* (the bearers of good news), *al-mursalat* (the sent ones), and *al-dhariyat* (the scattering ones). As for the punishment, they are *al-aqim* (the barren one) and *al-sarsar* (the piercing cold one), which are on land, and *al-'asif* (the violent one) and *al-qasif* (the crashing one), which are at sea."

﴿And that He may let you taste of His mercy﴾. Regarding this there are two interpretations (*ta'wilan*, interpretations):

The first: its coolness and pleasantness, said by al-Dahhak.

The second: the rain, said by Mujahid and Qatada.

﴿And that the ships may run﴾, meaning the boats.

﴿By His command﴾ may bear two meanings:

The first: by His power in making them move.

The second: by His mercy toward those who are on board.

﴿And that you may be grateful﴾, meaning for what He has enumerated of His blessings, so that you obey Him. For the servant's obedience to his Lord is part of his gratitude for His blessing, since there is no gratitude alongside disobedience, nor obedience alongside ingratitude for blessings.

His saying: ﴿And it was truly incumbent upon Us to help the believers﴾. Regarding this there are two meanings:

The first: the help of the prophets by answering their supplication against those among their peoples who denied them, said by Yahya ibn Sallam.

The second: the help of the believers by making it obligatory to defend their honour. Umm al-Darda' narrated, saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "There is no Muslim man who defends the honour of his brother except that it is a right upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to ward off the Fire of Hell from him on the Day of Resurrection." Then he recited this verse: ﴿And it was truly incumbent upon Us to help the believers﴾.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 30, verses 52–53:

His saying: ﴿So indeed you cannot make the dead hear﴾ has two interpretations:

The first: the dead are the disbelievers who die in disbelief, and they are the deaf who turned away from the guidance and so did not hear it. This was said by Yahya ibn Salam.

The second: this is a parable which Allah struck for the disbelievers, just as the dead person, when addressed, does not hear, and the deaf person, when called, does not hear. Likewise the disbeliever does not hear the admonition, because disbelief has caused him to die and misguidance has made him deaf.

His saying: ﴿And you cannot make the deaf hear the call when they turn away, retreating﴾. The deaf person does not hear the call whether it is addressed to him facing forward or turned away. However, when he is called while facing forward, he may understand a gesture even if he does not hear the voice. But when he is called while turned away, he understands neither the gesture nor hears the voice. Therefore his state while turned away is worse, so He reminded them of their worst state.

It was also said that it was revealed concerning the Banu Abd al-Dar.

؎ أُرِيتُ الشَّيْبَ مِن نُذُرِ المَنايا لِصاحِبِهِ وحَسْبَكَ مِن نَذِيرٍ

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 30, verse 55–57:

Allah's statement: ﴿And on the day the Hour is established, the criminals will swear﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "They are the disbelievers."

﴿That they had not remained but an hour﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions:

The first: [they had remained] in the world, briefly, for the sake of the world, in comparison with what they witnessed of the Hereafter. This was said by Qatadah.

The second: [they had remained] in their graves between their death and their resurrection. This was said by Yahya ibn Salam.

﴿Thus﴾, that is, in this manner. This was said by Ibn Jubayr.

﴿They used to be deluded﴾. Concerning this there are two views:

The first: they used to lie in the world. This was said by Qatadah.

The second: they used to turn people away from belief in the Resurrection in the world. This was said by Yahya ibn Salam.

Allah's statement: ﴿And those who were given knowledge and faith will say﴾. Concerning them there are two views:

The first: they are the angels. This was said by al-Kalbi.

The second: they are the People of the Book.

﴿And faith﴾ may carry two meanings:

The first: belief in the earlier Book without any distortion of it or alteration within it.

The second: belief in Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿You had remained in the Book of Allah until the Day of Resurrection﴾. Concerning this there are three views:

The first: you had remained in the knowledge of Allah. This was said by al-Farra' (al-Farra').

The second: you had remained by means of that whose explanation is in the Book of Allah. This was said by Ibn 'Isa.

The third: there is an inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in the sentence, its meaning being: ﴿And those who were given knowledge﴾ [in the Book of Allah] and faith will say, ﴿You had remained in the Book of Allah until the Day of Resurrection﴾. This was said by Qatadah.

Concerning ﴿you had remained﴾ there are two opinions:

The first: they remained in their graves.

(p-324) The second: in the world they were alive, and in their graves they were dead.

﴿This is the Day of Resurrection﴾, meaning that which you denied in the world.

﴿But you did not know﴾, that is, you did not know in the world that the Resurrection is true, and now you know that it is true.

Allah's statement: ﴿So on that Day﴾, meaning the Day of Resurrection.

﴿The excuse of those who wronged will not benefit them﴾, that is, their excuse with which they defended their denial.

﴿Nor will they be allowed to make amends﴾. Concerning this there are three views:

The first: they will not be reproached for their misdeeds. This was said by al-Naqqash.

The second: they will not be asked to repent. This was said by some of the later scholars.

The third: no request for amends (al-'utba) will be made of them, which would be that they be returned to the world so that they might make amends, that is, so that they might believe. This was said by Yahya ibn Salam.

The first: they will not be reproached for their misdeeds. This was said by al-Naqqash.

The second: they will not be asked to repent. This was said by some of the later scholars.

The third: no request for amends (al-'utba) will be made of them, which would be that they be returned to the world so that they might make amends, that is, so that they might believe. This was said by Yahya ibn Salam.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 30, verse 55–57:

Allah's statement: ﴿And on the day the Hour is established, the criminals will swear﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "They are the disbelievers."

﴿That they had not remained but an hour﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions:

The first: [they had remained] in the world, briefly, for the sake of the world, in comparison with what they witnessed of the Hereafter. This was said by Qatadah.

The second: [they had remained] in their graves between their death and their resurrection. This was said by Yahya ibn Salam.

﴿Thus﴾, that is, in this manner. This was said by Ibn Jubayr.

﴿They used to be deluded﴾. Concerning this there are two views:

The first: they used to lie in the world. This was said by Qatadah.

The second: they used to turn people away from belief in the Resurrection in the world. This was said by Yahya ibn Salam.

Allah's statement: ﴿And those who were given knowledge and faith will say﴾. Concerning them there are two views:

The first: they are the angels. This was said by al-Kalbi.

The second: they are the People of the Book.

﴿And faith﴾ may carry two meanings:

The first: belief in the earlier Book without any distortion of it or alteration within it.

The second: belief in Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿You had remained in the Book of Allah until the Day of Resurrection﴾. Concerning this there are three views:

The first: you had remained in the knowledge of Allah. This was said by al-Farra' (al-Farra').

The second: you had remained by means of that whose explanation is in the Book of Allah. This was said by Ibn 'Isa.

The third: there is an inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in the sentence, its meaning being: ﴿And those who were given knowledge﴾ [in the Book of Allah] and faith will say, ﴿You had remained in the Book of Allah until the Day of Resurrection﴾. This was said by Qatadah.

Concerning ﴿you had remained﴾ there are two opinions:

The first: they remained in their graves.

(p-324) The second: in the world they were alive, and in their graves they were dead.

﴿This is the Day of Resurrection﴾, meaning that which you denied in the world.

﴿But you did not know﴾, that is, you did not know in the world that the Resurrection is true, and now you know that it is true.

Allah's statement: ﴿So on that Day﴾, meaning the Day of Resurrection.

﴿The excuse of those who wronged will not benefit them﴾, that is, their excuse with which they defended their denial.

﴿Nor will they be allowed to make amends﴾. Concerning this there are three views:

The first: they will not be reproached for their misdeeds. This was said by al-Naqqash.

The second: they will not be asked to repent. This was said by some of the later scholars.

The third: no request for amends (al-'utba) will be made of them, which would be that they be returned to the world so that they might make amends, that is, so that they might believe. This was said by Yahya ibn Salam.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 30, verses 58–60:

His saying: ﴿So be patient. Indeed, the promise of Allah is true﴾. This is an address to the Prophet ﷺ, and it may have two meanings:

First: that the promise of Allah regarding your victory and support is true.

Second: that His promise regarding His vengeance against your enemies is true.

﴿And let them not unsettle you﴾. Concerning this there are three opinions:

First: "Let them not hasten you," as said by Ibn Shajara.

Second: "Let them not provoke you," as said by Yahya ibn Salam.

Third: "Let them not bring you down," as said by al-Naqqash.

﴿Those who have no certainty﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions:

(p-325) First: "Those who do not believe."

Second: "Those who do not affirm the resurrection and the recompense." Sa'id narrated from Qatada that a man from the Kharijites said to Ali, may Allah honour his face, while he was behind him in the dawn prayer: ﴿If you associate others with Allah, your deeds will surely be nullified﴾, to the end of the verse.

Ali said to him, while he was in the prayer: ﴿So be patient. Indeed, the promise of Allah is true, and let not those who have no certainty unsettle you﴾. And Allah knows best.
